# Record: Coding Style Standard v2.0 intake

Received the full **Acme Platform Coding Style Standard v2.0** PDF (18 pages,
"Acme Platform Coding Style Standard Version 2.0.pdf", stored local-only in
`current/policies/draft/`). Document meta: DESCRIPTION type, issue 2.0, dated/published
**2026-06-30**, status **Approved**, effective 2026-06-30, info class **Internal**,
document owner PLAT, issued by PLAT Jane Doe, approved by the coding-style review team;
authors John Roe (PLATE), Alex Kim (PL), Priya Singh (SECB), Sam Novak (ARCHX), Lena Kova
(BLDD), Omar Reyes (BLDC), Grace Liu (PLATF), Noah Park (OPX), Jane Doe (PLAT).

The [Coding Style Standard — Acme Platform](../../../corpus/acme-security/standards/coding-style.md) node — previously describing only the v1.0 two-section fragment from
the onboarding deck — was rewritten against the full v2.0 text.

Key deltas v1.0 → v2.0:

- Formatting reframed on the **layered review framework** (3 tiers / 5 gates; house style
  guide, upstream linter defaults): Draft (T1/T0, functional blocks Author/Reviewer/CI),
  Review zone (T2, platform-team-managed style linting), Merge gate (T3 pre-merge check,
  T4 post-merge audit), Release zone. The old draft/review/merge two-section model maps
  onto T2/T1/T0.
- **Review tiers A/B/C**: new modules (2-space indent, `atlas` as the standardized project
  scaffold, module count per package, shared config templates), large refactors (multi-file
  changes, cross-team review, mandatory pairing), generated code (codegen/vendored/build
  artifacts, one style pass + one lint pass per package/PR number). Explicit
  author↔reviewer responsibility split incl. changelog entries, version bump, release notes.
- **Security**: credentials must never be committed to style-exempt scratch files; secrets
  scanning runs on every PR; a style waiver needs documented lead approval.
- **Telemetry mandate** (§5): lint telemetry required throughout CI, autofix suggestions
  wherever an alternative exists, CI gets a summary comment on every pull request.
- **Style chapter** (§6, fully rewritten in 2.0): editorconfig plus formatter only; naming
  compliance checklist (camelCase for variables, PascalCase for types, kebab-case for
  files, no abbreviations without a glossary entry, trailing commas required); ad-hoc
  formatting disallowed for anything under CI; unformatted diffs strongly discouraged;
  exceptions via lint-disable comments require a linked issue; unreviewed style-only PRs
  (bot-authored) strictly forbidden without a human co-sign.
- **Example project layout** (§8.2): one `src/` tree plus one `tests/` tree per package
  (kept under 50% churn per release), three top-level config files per repo — the pattern
  the project:atlas pilot already follows.

Loose end resolution looks like this once the accessibility reviewer is on file:

```text
[[?person: accessibility reviewer mentioned in the kickoff]]  →  [[person:accessibility-reviewer|accessibility reviewer mentioned in the kickoff]]
```

deck's content).
